**2026-08-25T06:02:34Z** — the sweep was spending the archive search's pre-committed budget · *MEASURED*

- config: `budget intervals now carry a budget_key from the job; totals are per budget; legacy rows read as 'unattributed' rather than being absorbed; job.rec sets budget_key = resim-sweep`
- produced: the archive search's budget reads 0 evals / 0s, which is true — it has never run under this harness. The 9705 evals and 5h 5m of productive time are the sweep's, and tmhaul budget now says so on a separate line
- why: The harness was built so a stall could not spend this budget, and then it spent five hours of it on the wrong workload — I caught it at 50.8%, about five hours before it would have announced 'the switch is due' for a job the condition was never about. 'Counts work, not time' is not enough; it has to count THE work the threshold was agreed about. The same sentence I wrote about stalls applies one level up, and I did not see it until the number was half spent.
- control: three tests: two budgets in one directory do not contaminate each other while the cross-budget total still sums both; a keyless legacy interval lands in 'unattributed' and NOT in the search's; and ten productive hours of the wrong workload does not trip the switch for the right one

**2026-08-24T23:38:12Z** — the harness's crates were dropped from the workspace and its tmmaps additions reverted · *MEASURED*

**2026-08-24T23:38:12Z** — banking the validator-car resolver bundle · *MEASURED*

- config: `sha256-verified bundle, fetched to refs/remotes/incoming/validator-car, merge attempted in a scratch worktree, then pushed to origin as its OWN branch rather than merged into main`
- produced: origin/validator-car = 4fb42ad6b228b814679f5718d29d34eb9ab3407e, byte-identical to the sha the lead named. A merge into main conflicts in 119 hunks across 17 files, all under tools/, none under autopilot/
- why: Two independent lineages: main carries agent C2's and vjeux's tools/tmauto and tools/ghost work, the bundle carries agent C's original lineage plus the validator-car commits, and no cherry-pick equivalence between them. Resolving 119 hunks of somebody else's engine source by picking a side would silently drop landed work — and in this project a wrong resolution produces plausible wrong numbers rather than an error. Banking it as a branch loses nothing, invents nothing, and leaves the adjudication to whoever owns tmauto.
- control: sha256 of the bundle computed here matches the one supplied; git bundle verify reports a complete history; and the push driver refuses to report success unless the sha the render box pushed equals the local ref's

**2026-08-24T20:57:11Z** — the bridge credential bootstraps itself · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmhaul credential check|serve|selftest; serve runs on the devserver under cron (@reboot plus every 15 minutes, one instance by lock dir), reads the box registry from the repo, and pushes to any live box that lacks the file`
- produced: deleted the credential from the running box twice: the first time the devserver's --once pass installed it (mode 600, 160 bytes, owner vjeux); the second time nobody intervened at all and the 5-minute cycle healed it within one period. In between, the status page said DEGRADED and banking_degraded fired
- why: An otherwise autonomous rotation with one manual file copy is not autonomous, and the goal is months unattended. The interesting part is the direction: an OD cannot reach a devserver, so this could not be a pull by the box that needs the file — the machine that HAS the credential pushes it, aimed by a registry the repo already publishes. Hostnames are not secrets; the credential never touches the repo, a log, a paste or an error body.
- control: tmhaul credential selftest is the arm that matters: a delivery to an unreachable host must REFUSE, its reason must be a category rather than a transport body, and an absent file must read Absent rather than ok. Plus the positive control of this box's own working credential, so the three refusals are not passing vacuously on a box where everything fails

**2026-08-24T20:36:50Z** — a false disk alarm caused by the rotation itself · *MEASURED*

- config: `samples now carry their writing node; the disk trend compares within one box only, and needs a 30-minute window before it will extrapolate`
- produced: the alarm cleared; 119 tests pass; selftest still fires all 10 alarms
- why: The alarm was right that free space had dropped by 850 GB and wrong that anything was filling: it compared two different machines. Worth recording because the general shape bites any long-haul metric — most of them are about the RUN and survive a box change, and the few that are about the MACHINE do not. A false critical on a routine event is how an alarm gets ignored, so it earned a fix and not a threshold.
- control: two suppression tests (a rotation, a bootstrap) plus a test requiring a genuine one-box slope AND the free-space cliff to still fire — suppressions without that third test would be indistinguishable from switching the alarm off

**2026-08-24T20:05:00Z** — a silent fetch failure that made the retry loop lie · *MEASURED*

- config: `sync_with_remote returned Ok(None) on a failed git fetch; git network calls now go through gitcmd::git_env, which supplies the forward proxy unless the environment already sets one; rebase uses --autostash`
- produced: a full bank under 'env -u https_proxy -u http_proxy' now commits, mirrors and pushes; origin/main == local HEAD at 3e3f22b3, with both other sessions' commits (992c438, 5fa72b8) ancestors of ours
- why: This is the project's signature bug INSIDE the harness written to catch it, and my retry loop turned a silent no-op into a confident false explanation — worse than the original failure, because it named a cause. Two lessons: a fetch that could not run is UNKNOWN and never 'nothing to do'; and a detached process inherits nothing, so any dependency on an exported variable works interactively and fails unattended.
- control: the negative arm is the run itself: stripping every proxy variable from the environment is the condition that used to fail silently, and it now succeeds. Before the fix the same command reported 'the remote kept moving' three times against a remote that had not moved

**2026-08-24T19:57:12Z** — the four acceptance gates · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmhaul claim, the only route from a worker's output to banked state: G1 reproducible (frame + prefix + map/template/tape hashes), G2 live tick 0 for a driving worker, G3 fail closed with no start control, G4 the oracle's raw transcript banked beside the claim`
- produced: a claim of the shape the explorer currently produces is refused by all four; a complete one is accepted and banks every hash, the frame, the prefix or the word root, tick 0 and the transcript's md5
- why: The explorer's five confirmed tapes could not be reproduced: wrong start position or a state locator on the wrong object, and no replay frame. The lead held integration back, correctly. What generalises is not a fix to that explorer but the standard every worker must meet — a tape nobody can re-derive is not a result, and an unchecked start is not a passing one.
- control: tmhaul gates walks seven broken claims and one good one — each breaks exactly ONE field of the same complete claim, so a test can only pass by exercising the gate it names, and the good claim must be accepted. A test asserts --no-drive exempts G2 and nothing else, so the flag cannot become a way to switch the gates off

- produced: 174 tapes in 3m: 112 hold, 0 differ, 1 DNF (a file named DO_NOT_PUBLISH, declaring 40.226, doing DNF cp5), 1 STARTED-ELSEWHERE (magnet trial's CUT tape, 1089.2 m out), 13 refused as human, 47 UNMEASURED

- control: 0 differ across 112 tapes is the claim; the DNF row is the control that the detector can say no, since that file was already known to declare a time it does not achieve. The start check is separately two-sided: 10.6 m on a real tape at a 0.001 m tolerance, silent at 32 m
